title: The globular cluster NGC 104
caption: The globular cluster 47 Tucanae (NGC 104), imaged by ESO's 1-metre Schmidt Telescope
celestial: NGC 104 · constellation Tucana · about 15000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: This colour-corrected image shows NGC 104, better known as 47 Tucanae, the second-largest and second-brightest globular cluster in Earth's night sky. A globular cluster is a tight, roughly spherical grouping of stars bound together by gravity, and this one holds a great many stars.

The light for the picture was gathered in 1986 with ESO's 1-metre Schmidt Telescope at La Silla Observatory in Chile. A Schmidt telescope is designed to photograph wide areas of sky at once, which makes it well suited to capturing a large, bright cluster like this in a single frame.
The telescope has since been decommissioned, so this image is also a small piece of observatory history, a record made by an instrument that no longer observes.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (29.72 x 37.56 arcminutes) and distance (15000 light years), the frame spans roughly 130 × 164 light-years. Its light set out about 15,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This is a colour-corrected visible-light image from ESO's 1-metre Schmidt Telescope. The source does not list the filters or publish the colour mapping.
understand.eye: The telescope gathers far more light than the eye, recording stars too faint to see directly.
